title: Holy orders
hook: deacons, priests and bishops ordained by the laying on of hands

segments.voice: Yesterday, extreme unction, the anointing of the sick. Your line was the sick are not forgotten.

Partway through an ordination Mass, a young man in a white robe walks to the front of a packed cathedral and lies down. Flat on the floor, face down, arms at his sides. The congregation kneels and sings a long list of saints' names, asking each to pray for him. It goes on for minutes. Somewhere in the pews, his mother may be in tears. It's startling to see in a church: a man giving his whole body to the ground before he's given a job.
screen: `A YOUNG MAN LIES FACE DOWN.` → `A LONG LIST OF SAINTS.` → `HIS WHOLE BODY TO THE GROUND.`

segments.voice: Ordination comes from the Latin ordo, an order or rank, the word Romans used for the groups that made up their society. The sacrament is called holy orders, plural, because there are three: deacons, priests and bishops. The names are Greek. Deacon is diakonos, a servant, someone who waits on tables. Priest comes, through old English, from presbyteros, an elder. Bishop comes from episkopos, an overseer. Each is a kind of serving. The sign is very old: hands laid on the head in silence. In Acts, seven men are chosen to care for widows, whom Catholic tradition counts as the first deacons, and in the Douay-Rheims, "they praying, imposed hands upon them." The letters to Timothy also recall a gift that came through the laying on of hands. At an ordination today, the bishop lays his hands on the candidate's head without a word, then prays the prayer of consecration. At a priest's ordination, every priest present lays on hands too. Catholics believe this sacrament, like baptism, marks a person for good. Priests celebrate the Eucharist and hear confessions; deacons baptize, preach, witness marriages and serve the poor; bishops lead a diocese and ordain others. In the Latin Church, priests and bishops are normally celibate, while permanent deacons can be married, and Eastern Catholic churches have married priests. The Church ordains only men, and teaches that it has no authority to ordain women as priests; some Catholics hope that will change. Other Christians understand ministry differently: the Orthodox keep the same three orders; Anglicans keep bishops, priests and deacons too; other Protestant churches ordain ministers but generally don't count ordination as a sacrament.
screen: `ORDO: AN ORDER, A RANK.` · `SERVANT, ELDER, OVERSEER.` · `HANDS LAID ON IN SILENCE.` · `MARKED FOR GOOD, TO SERVE.` · then, large: `CALLED TO SERVE.`

segments.voice: Make a short litany of your own, like the one sung over the man on the floor: one name for each breath. If you pray and know some saints, use theirs, Mary, Joseph, Peter, and answer each quietly, pray for us. If you don't, use the names of people who served you well, a teacher, a nurse, a grandmother, with a moment of thanks for each.
Ordination. From the Latin for an order. Deacons, priests and bishops, made by the laying on of hands to serve. Today's word.
Your line: called to serve. Hands in silence, for a life of service. See you tomorrow.
